clue.text: Local souvenir stores in France, for instance

indicators.note: something that stores another holds it inside, so the souvenir word keeps the local inside it

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake or memento
a local is a British word for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: Shops near a French tourist site selling local trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective for the souvenirs; it is the noun for a nearby pub, which goes inside RELIC.
explanation.definitionFit: France is one example of a state governed without a monarch, by elected representatives.

clue.text: Stopped one who rejects accepted truth turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a denier refuses to accept established facts, as a climate denier does

explanation.surface: A sceptic arrives and is halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein a horse is to check or halt it with the reins, so the past tense means stopped.

clue.text: Choose, say, to collect money for strike activity

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the example abbreviation holds the money word

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A union member decides to gather donations for the strike fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' has the example abbreviation enclose the slang money word; 'say' signals an example, as so often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing outside a workplace to dissuade others from entering is the classic action of strikers.

clue.text: Live overlooking South Wales town or lower down

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part overlooking another sits above it

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
Neath is a town in South Wales, near Swansea

explanation.surface: Choosing between living with a view over a Welsh town or further down the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated under something else is lower down than it.

clue.text: Unsuitable interest surrounds origins of environmental protesters

indicators.note: the interest abbreviation surrounds, that is encloses, the picked letters

parts.note: INT is the standard abbreviation for interest in finance

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the first letter of each of the two following words is taken

explanation.surface: Climate activists' concerns judged out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or fitness for a task, so it can describe something unsuitable or inappropriate.

clue.text: Sweet-looking child Bruce spoiled outside hospital

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit outside the hospital letter, enclosing it
spoiled suggests the letters of the name are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Little Bruce, a pampered child, is waiting outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges BRUCE to CERUB, which goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are the chubby angelic infants of paintings, hence any child with an innocent, appealing face.

clue.text: More convenient hotel, above a run-down diner

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece above another comes before it

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: run-down means dilapidated, signalling the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a hotel handier than the shabby diner nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means conveniently placed or useful, so the comparative means more convenient.

clue.text: Dish from Ankara I tasted

indicators.note: the letters come from within the run of words, read straight through

explanation.surface: A traveller recalls a dish sampled in the Turkish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or other vegetables.

clue.text: Once party is over, they may have a deflated look?

definitions.text: Once party is over, they may have a deflated look?

parts.words: Once party is over, they may have a deflated look?
parts.note: partygoers might look deflated afterwards, but it is the inflatable decorations that literally lose their air

explanation.surface: After the celebration, the guests look glum.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated rubber decorations at parties shrink and sag as the air escapes over the following days.

clue.text: Brawny American couple oddly beset by ruin

indicators.note: the inner letters are surrounded, beset on all sides, by the ruin word

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: oddly takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of the word

explanation.surface: A strong pair from the States beset by disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd-numbered letters of 'couple', not its sense; 'beset by' puts them, after the American abbreviation, within the ruin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawny means physically strong with well-developed muscles.

clue.text: Student pursues trendy antiques, once treated as unimportant

indicators.note: the student letter pursues, that is follows on after, the rest

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter, a crossword standard for student

explanation.surface: A student follows fashion in antiques once dismissed as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no consequence is trivial and not important.

clue.text: Polished part of table between each set of books

indicators.note: the table part sits between the two letters of the each abbreviation

parts.note: a leg is one part of a table
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A refined table leg wedged between volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined, as is something polished in style or manners.

clue.text: Musical, fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
ago means in the past, earlier

explanation.surface: A stage show that was once stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kander and Ebb's stage show about jazz-age murderesses is one well-known example of a musical.

clue.text: Just terrible losing first source of finance

indicators.note: losing means the following letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: frightful means terrible or dreadful

indicators.note: the first source is the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Simply awful to lose your main source of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful means fair and legitimate, as a just claim is.

clue.text: Fine radio exposure for song getting just treatment

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
airplay is the broadcasting a record gets on the radio

explanation.surface: A record finally gets the broadcasts it deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair play is the principle of honest, even-handed dealing with everyone.

clue.text: Tree Truro wants to protect

indicators.note: the outer words protect, that is shield, the letters held within them

explanation.surface: The Cornish city wishes to save a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Truro is the county town of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with red berries, is a small tree of the rose family.

clue.text: Old MP hugs excited girl, one aboard merry-go-round

indicators.note: the politician word hugs, or wraps round, the other letters

parts.note: the Whigs were an old British party, forerunners of the Liberals

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one; aboard means it comes along with the shuffled letters

explanation.surface: A former politician embraces a thrilled girl riding a fairground carousel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the girl's letters, and the numeral one joins them inside the old party name. 'one aboard' reads as a rider, but the definition is just 'merry-go-round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirligig is an old word for a carousel or any spinning toy.

clue.text: Angry with crook producing weapon

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
a crook is a bend, as is a bow

explanation.surface: Someone furious with a villain produces a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but here it is a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a bow mounted on a stock that shoots bolts.

clue.text: Strict and clear ruling ultimately Italy breaks

indicators.note: the inner letters break into the clear word, splitting it

parts.note: to rid is to clear or free

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, taking the last letter

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A clear and strict ruling that Italy ultimately violates.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means inflexible, as strict rules are.

clue.text: Exchange views on son supporting athletics event

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath

parts.note: the discus is a throwing event in athletics
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Parents talk about their son's track-and-field event.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk something over is to share opinions about it.

clue.text: Conservative PM's beginning to expel foreign nationals

indicators.note: the beginning, the opening letter, is to be expelled

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Conservative Prime Minister in the 19th century

explanation.surface: A Tory leader's first act is to deport foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of the state in the Middle East are, to a British setter, nationals of a foreign country.

clue.text: Vintage coin found inside empty Eastbourne train

indicators.note: the coin is found inside the two letters left
empty removes the inner letters, leaving the first and last

parts.note: the ducat was an old European gold coin

explanation.surface: An antique coin discovered on a deserted train to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastbourne is a seaside town on England's south coast. 'empty' leaves EE.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach or school them.

clue.text: Notice that lady's poodle at last finding stick

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
her means belonging to that lady

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a woman's poodle finally finds a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fixed to something.

clue.text: Last drink delays retirement to bed

parts.note: to last is to stay or endure
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A nightcap puts off going to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective, final, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not go to sleep at the usual hour is putting off going to bed.

clue.text: Main artery, part of that road going north

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means the letters run upwards
part of signals letters taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A trunk route heads north along a stretch of road.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the largest artery, carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Group of players defending centre for silliest foul

indicators.note: the team word defends, or surrounds, the middle letters

parts.note: a squad is a group of players in a team

indicators.note: centre takes the middle two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A team protecting the clumsiest player commits a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid means filthy and dirty, as something foul is.

clue.text: Father needs new security alarm, perhaps

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Dad wants a new burglar alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A security alarm is one example of a device that wails a warning sound.

clue.text: Surprisingly gain lumber trade in place of what's disappeared?

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected outcome, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A timber business unexpectedly makes a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of the Atlantic is famed for ships and aircraft that vanished there mysteriously.

clue.text: Fish river area, visiting West Sussex regularly

indicators.note: the river and area letters are visiting, staying inside, the rest
regularly takes every other letter, 1st, 3rd and 5th

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An angler's spot: a river area in West Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives SSE from SUSSEX; RA goes between W and SSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrasses are a family of brightly coloured sea fish.

clue.text: Persuade Nigel I've changed

indicators.note: changed signals the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: A confession that one has talked Nigel round.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or cajole someone into doing something.
